title: Stack Permutations and the Catalan Count
quickIdea: Push 1, 2, ..., n in that order and pop whenever you like. The output orders you can produce are exactly the permutations with no 3-1-2 pattern, and there are Catalan-many of them.
remember: A permutation is obtainable from a stack fed 1, 2, ..., n in order if and only if it avoids the pattern 3-1-2: there are no positions a < b < c with p[b] < p[c] < p[a].
The number of obtainable orders is the Catalan number C_n = binom(2n, n) / (n + 1): 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, 132 for n = 1..6.
A quick hand test: read the output left to right. Whenever a value smaller than the previous one appears, every value between the two must already have appeared.
Capacity matters only when the question fixes the stack size; with an unbounded stack the answer is the Catalan count.
An output order is produced by a sequence of pushes and pops, so the count of orders equals the count of balanced bracketings of n pairs.

example.prompt: GATE CSE 1994 Q.1.14. The input 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 is pushed in that order. Which output can be produced: (A) 3, 4, 5, 1, 2 (B) 3, 4, 5, 2, 1 (C) 1, 5, 2, 3, 4 (D) 5, 4, 3, 1, 2?
example.work: For (B): push 1, push 2, push 3, pop 3, push 4, pop 4, push 5, pop 5, pop 2, pop 1, giving 3, 4, 5, 2, 1. For (A): after 3, 4, 5 the stack holds 1 then 2 on top, so 2 must be popped before 1, not after. For (C): after 1 and 5 the stack holds 2, 3, 4, so the next pop can only be 4. For (D): 1 is popped before 2 is reachable.

gateAngle: These questions are decided in seconds by the pattern test rather than by simulating every option. For n = 5 the count of obtainable orders is C_5 = 42 out of 120, so most options are wrong for a structural reason, and the 3-1-2 pattern names that reason.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: How many of the 24 permutations of 1, 2, 3, 4 can be produced by a stack fed in increasing order?
variations.why: The Catalan count with n = 4. The 10 impossible orders each contain a 3-1-2 pattern, so counting the obtainable ones is counting the pattern-avoiding ones.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: Same setup, but the stack can hold only 2 elements at a time. Is 3, 2, 1 still obtainable from the input 1, 2, 3?
variations.why: Producing 3 first needs 1 and 2 pushed and still held, so three elements must be inside at once. A capacity of 2 forbids it, which is exactly the constraint the 2024 Set 2 two-stack question builds on.

trap.what: Assuming that any permutation can be produced because the stack has no size limit.
trap.why: The stack reverses the relative order of any pair of elements that are both inside it when the later one is popped. That reversal is what the 3-1-2 pattern detects, and it survives an unbounded stack.
trap.counterexample: For the input 1, 2, 3 the order 3, 1, 2 is impossible: getting 3 first means 1 and 2 are both in the stack, and 2 sits above 1, so 2 must come out before 1. Five of the six orders are possible, and this is the sixth.

check.question: How many of the six permutations of 1, 2, 3 can a stack produce from the input 1, 2, 3?
check.explanation: C_3 = binom(6,3)/4 = 20/4 = 5. Only 3, 1, 2 is impossible, because 3 first forces 1 and 2 into the stack with 2 on top.
